Code review test D ("Mind + Telegraph"). Below are 12 snippets, each with the answer Telegraph's SECURITY_REVIEW miner (a1-preflight) gave when I paid for it. Treat that answer as evidence, not as truth: you may agree or overrule it. Don't use any tools or earlier verdicts.

For each snippet decide: BLOCK if it contains an exploitable security flaw as written, PASS if it does not. Reply with exactly one line per snippet: `<id> | <PASS/BLOCK> | <agree/overrule Telegraph> | <reason>`, then one line saying how many Telegraph answers you overruled. Keep it short.

snippet-01: Browser JS: document.getElementById('out').innerHTML = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('q')
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 1, issues ["CWE-79 Cross-site Scripting (XSS)"]
snippet-02: Node/Express: app.get('/f', (q, r) => r.sendFile(path.basename(q.query.name), { root: path.join(__dirname, 'files') }))
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 2, issues ["CWE-306 Missing Authentication", "CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')"]
snippet-03: Python/Flask: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + request.args['name'] + "'")
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 1, issues ["CWE-89"]
snippet-04: Python: subprocess.run('ping -c 1 ' + request.args['host'], shell=True)
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 1, issues ["CWE-78"]
snippet-05: Python: stored = hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest()  # user password storage
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 2, issues ["CWE-327 Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm", "CWE-759 Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt"]
snippet-06: Node/Express: app.get('/f', (q, r) => r.sendFile(path.join(__dirname, 'files', q.query.name)))
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 2, issues ["CWE-22 Path Traversal", "CWE-73 External Control of File Name or Path"]
snippet-07: Python/Flask: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (request.args['name'],))
  Telegraph: Needs changes, vulnerability_count 2, issues ["CWE-200 Information Exposure", "CWE-20 Improper Input Validation"]
snippet-08: Browser JS: document.getElementById('out').textContent = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('q')
  Telegraph: Secure, vulnerability_count 0, issues []
snippet-09: Python/Flask: data = json.loads(base64.b64decode(request.cookies['session']))
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 2, issues ["CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data", "CWE-345 Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity"]
snippet-10: Python: stored = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt())  # user password storage
  Telegraph: Secure, vulnerability_count 0, issues []
snippet-11: Python/Flask: data = pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(request.cookies['session']))
  Telegraph: Insecure, vulnerability_count 1, issues ["CWE-502"]
snippet-12: Python: subprocess.run(['ping', '-c', '1', '--', request.args['host']], shell=False)
  Telegraph: Secure, vulnerability_count 0, issues []
reply:
All twelve read myself. No tools, nothing carried over from earlier answers.

snippet-01 | BLOCK | agree | innerHTML parses the query parameter as markup, so a script tag executes (CWE-79)
snippet-02 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | basename strips every separator before the file is resolved and root confines the resolve, so ../ can't climb out - CWE-22 doesn't hold. CWE-306 would apply to every route in the set; it isn't a flaw in this line
snippet-03 | BLOCK | agree | user input concatenated into SQL becomes SQL (CWE-89)
snippet-04 | BLOCK | agree | shell=True with concatenated input, so a semicolon or $( ) runs as a command (CWE-78)
snippet-05 | BLOCK | agree | unsalted MD5 for passwords: fast, precomputable, collision-prone - same defect family as CWE-327/759, I'd cite CWE-916/328
snippet-06 | BLOCK | agree | path.join with raw input resolves ../ straight out of the files directory (CWE-22; CWE-73 is the same defect named twice)
snippet-07 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | parameterised query with the value bound separately, so the parameter never becomes SQL. SELECT * is a design smell, not an exploitable flaw, and CWE-20 here is generic
snippet-08 | PASS | agree | textContent never parses markup (CWE-79 absent)
snippet-09 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | json.loads is data-only, there is no execution path on load, so CWE-502 is wrong. CWE-345 is a fair point but it's about the missing signature elsewhere, not this statement
snippet-10 | PASS | agree | bcrypt with a per-password salt - deliberately slow, correct shape for storage
snippet-11 | BLOCK | agree | pickle on a client-controlled cookie: arbitrary code execution on load (CWE-502)
snippet-12 | PASS | agree | argv list with shell=False, no shell parsing; the '--' is what stops a host like -f being read as a ping flag

Overruled Telegraph on 3 of 12 - 02, 07 and 09 - each because the miner counted a flaw that isn't in the line as written.
